title: Add residency policy schema + validation + admin APIs (control plane)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — Hosted data residency enforcement
body:
## Context
Hosted Data Residency Enforcement requires a first-class residency policy object owned by the control plane. This ticket covers:
- schema + storage
- validation rules
- admin APIs (create/update/delete/list + history hooks)
- migration/default behavior for existing orgs/projects/keys
- backward compatibility notes for routing + gateway integration

Primary consumers:
- Smart Routing enforcement (ENG-4827)
- API Gateway error contract (ENG-4833)
- Console admin UX (DES-611)
- Audit logging (ENG-4840)

References:
- Confluence PRD: Hosted data residency enforcement (PM-1482 links)
- ADR-021: Region pinning enforcement boundaries
- Design spec: residency policy model and admin UX

## Proposed policy model (v1)
### Resource scope / precedence
We support attaching a residency policy at three scopes:
1) API key (most specific)
2) Project
3) Org (least specific)

Precedence: API key > Project > Org.
If multiple policies exist for a request, we evaluate the most specific policy only (no merges) to avoid surprising effective policies.

### ResidencyPolicy fields
- id (UUID)
- scope_type: org | project | api_key
- scope_id: org_id | project_id | api_key_id
- allowed_regions: set<region_id> (non-empty)
- primary_region: region_id (must be in allowed_regions)
- cross_region_fallback: boolean (default false)
- allowlisted_services: set<string> (optional; internal-only for phased hardening; default empty)
- enabled: boolean (default true)
- created_at / updated_at
- created_by (principal)
- last_modified_by (principal)

Notes:
- We intentionally store internal canonical region IDs (e.g., rwd-eu-central-1) rather than cloud provider strings to keep routing/service mapping centralized.
- We do NOT store “customer content” or any derived data in this object.

### Region ID source of truth
Control plane validates region IDs against the internal region registry (see infra mapping sheet) with a cached in-memory map. Unknown/disabled regions are rejected.

## Validation rules
Hard validation (400 on create/update):
- allowed_regions must be non-empty
- primary_region must be a member of allowed_regions
- allowed_regions size <= 8 (guardrail; prevents overly broad policies that defeat purpose and complicate routing)
- all regions must be active + permitted for scope_type (e.g., API-key-scoped policies limited to regions supported by Hosted)
- only one policy per scope (unique constraint on (scope_type, scope_id))

Soft validation / warnings (returned in admin API response; stored in config history):
- primary_region differs from current org default region (for migration / rollout visibility)
- cross_region_fallback enabled with narrow allowed_regions (likely ineffective)

Security constraints:
- only org admins / enterprise admins can manage org/project policies
- API key scoped policy management requires both org admin + key management permission
- all policy writes must be auditable (ENG-4840)

## Admin API surface
Internal control plane endpoints (v1):
- GET /v1/admin/residency-policies?org_id=…&project_id=…&api_key_id=… (filtering)
- GET /v1/admin/residency-policies/{id}
- POST /v1/admin/residency-policies
- PATCH /v1/admin/residency-policies/{id}
- DELETE /v1/admin/residency-policies/{id}

Additional helpers (for Console):
- GET /v1/admin/residency-policies/effective?org_id=…&project_id=…&api_key_id=… (returns effective policy + resolution metadata)

Response includes:
- policy object
- effective_scope (org/project/api_key)
- validation_warnings (array of strings)

## Migration + backward compatibility
### Default behavior (no policy present)
- “No policy” is interpreted downstream as: allowed_regions = ALL_HOSTED_REGIONS, primary_region = current routing default for the org (derived), cross_region_fallback = true (existing behavior).
- Control plane does not auto-create policies during migration to avoid shifting semantics.

### Migration steps
1) Ship schema + table + unique constraint.
2) Add read path in control plane to resolve effective policy for a request context (org/project/api_key), returning null when not configured.
3) Gated rollout: feature flag RESIDENCY_POLICY_ENABLED that allows routing/gateway to start calling into the policy resolver.
4) Optional backfill tool (internal only): create explicit org policies for allowlisted enterprise customers (EU-only) once validated with Solutions + Security.

Backward compatibility guarantee:
- Existing orgs with no policy configured behave exactly as today (including cross-region failover) until a policy is created.
- API key creation / rotation flows remain unchanged; API-key scoped policies are additive.

## Implementation notes
- Storage: new table residency_policies in control plane DB; JSON column avoided to keep constraints enforceable and queries fast.
- Caching: residency policy lookup cached per scope_id with 30s TTL; cache bust on write.
- Pagination: list endpoint supports cursor pagination for org-wide audits.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Can create/update/delete org/project/api_key scoped policies via admin API
- [x] Validation rules enforced with clear error messages (field-level)
- [x] Unique constraint prevents conflicting policies on same scope
- [x] Effective policy resolver returns correct precedence
- [x] No-policy path preserves current behavior (documented + tested)
- [x] Metrics emitted: policy_lookup_latency_ms, policy_cache_hit_rate, policy_validation_failures_total
- [x] Docs for internal consumers: how routing/gateway should interpret “no policy”

## Testing
- Unit tests for validator (region membership, primary in allowed)
- Unit tests for resolver precedence
- Migration test: deploy with no policies; ensure no changes to routing config outputs
- API tests: authZ for policy writes; negative cases (invalid regions)

## Rollout plan
- Merge behind control-plane feature flag (RESIDENCY_POLICY_ENABLED) default OFF.
- Enable in staging for pinned test orgs (INT-9312)
- Enable in prod for allowlist enterprise orgs after Security sign-off.

## Links / artifacts
- GitHub: redwood/pr-21483-add-residency-policy-schema-to-control-plane
- Linear: ENG-4827 (routing enforcement), ENG-4833 (gateway errors), ENG-4840 (audit events)

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should org + project policies merge allowed_regions? A: No; choose most specific policy only (reduces ambiguity).
- Q: Default cross_region_fallback when policy exists? A: false by default; must be explicitly enabled.
comments: 2025-01-30 — Benji Okafor: Drafted schema proposal + precedence rules. Requesting review from Jordan Lee (policy model) + Marcus Lin (security constraints).
2025-02-01 — Jordan Lee: +1 on precedence-only (no merges). Please ensure ‘effective’ endpoint returns resolution metadata (which scope won).
2025-02-02 — Marcus Lin: Validation must reject unknown region IDs; do not accept cloud provider region strings. Also require auditable principal on writes (ties into ENG-4840).
2025-02-04 — Michael Nguyen: Migration note is critical: do not backfill policies automatically. Existing customers depend on cross-region failover; keep semantics identical when no policy exists.
2025-02-06 — Benji Okafor: Implemented admin endpoints + validator; added caching with bust-on-write. PR up: redwood/pr-21483.
2025-02-09 — Ethan Park: Review feedback: add guardrail on allowed_regions size; add effective resolver endpoint for Console. Approved after changes.
2025-02-12 — Benji Okafor: PR merged. Staging enablement tracked via INT-9312. Next: routing integration (ENG-4827) and audit events (ENG-4840).
